note: Curated by the Mosaic team. Book blurbs are written for this site; cover art comes from the publishers. Regenerate with the harvest scripts in assets/resources/ — see docs/resources-data.md.

groups.title: New Believer: What Is Christianity All About?

books.title: What Is the Gospel?
books.author: Greg Gilbert
books.description: A short, plain answer to the question the whole faith rests on. Gilbert walks through God, humanity, Christ and our response, keeping to what the Bible itself says the good news is.

books.title: Who Is Jesus?
books.author: Greg Gilbert
books.description: An introduction for anyone who wants to know who Jesus actually was before deciding what to make of him. Gilbert works from the Gospel accounts rather than from later assumptions about them.

books.title: Am I Really a Christian?
books.author: Mike McKinley
books.description: A frank book for people who assume they already know the answer. McKinley tests the question against what Scripture says marks a genuine believer, written with warmth rather than suspicion.

groups.title: Where Can I Find Answers for My Skepticism?

books.title: The Reason for God
books.author: Timothy Keller
books.description: Keller takes the seven objections he heard most often as a Manhattan pastor, gives each one its full weight, and then makes the positive case for Christian faith. Written for the genuinely unconvinced.

books.title: Making Sense of God
books.author: Timothy Keller
books.description: The book Keller wrote for people not yet ready for The Reason for God. It asks whether secularism can actually deliver the meaning, freedom and identity it promises, before arguing anything about Christianity.

books.title: Evidence That Demands a Verdict
books.author: Josh McDowell and Sean McDowell
books.description: A reference volume rather than a read-through: manuscript evidence, archaeology and historical testimony assembled for people whose questions are evidential. Revised with Sean McDowell for contemporary objections.

groups.title: Spirituality: How Do I Live as a Christian?

books.title: The Discipline of Grace
books.author: Jerry Bridges
books.description: Bridges works out how grace and effort fit together in daily Christian life, arguing that the gospel is not just how you begin but how you keep going. A steady, unhurried book.

books.title: Now That I'm a Christian
books.author: C. Michael Patton
books.description: Written for the first year of faith. Patton covers what a new Christian is expected to already understand but usually doesn't: the Trinity, Scripture, prayer, church and doubt.

books.title: Desiring God
books.author: John Piper
books.description: Piper's central argument, that God is most glorified in us when we are most satisfied in him. Reframes duty-driven faith around joy. Dense in places and worth the slower reading.

books.title: Celebration of Discipline
books.author: Richard J. Foster
books.description: The modern classic on spiritual practice, covering meditation, prayer, fasting, study, simplicity, solitude, submission, service, confession, worship, guidance and celebration. Written across traditions rather than from one.

groups.title: What Does It Mean to Be a Disciple of Jesus?

books.title: The Cost of Discipleship
books.author: Dietrich Bonhoeffer
books.description: Bonhoeffer's account of what following Christ actually costs, written in Germany in 1937 and shaped by that pressure. The source of the distinction between cheap grace and costly grace.

books.title: Multiply
books.author: Francis Chan
books.description: A workbook built for two people to use together, on the assumption that disciples are made by other disciples rather than by programmes. Structured for someone discipling a newer believer.

books.title: Radical
books.author: David Platt
books.description: Platt sets the American dream against what Jesus asked of his followers and argues the two have quietly merged. A confrontational book, written by a pastor about his own congregation.

groups.title: How Do I Read the Bible?

books.title: God's Big Picture
books.author: Vaughan Roberts
books.description: Traces the storyline of Scripture through the theme of God's kingdom, showing how sixty-six books hold together as one narrative. Short, and the usual first recommendation for whole-Bible orientation.

books.title: How to Read the Bible for All Its Worth
books.author: Gordon D. Fee and Douglas Stuart
books.description: The standard guide to reading each biblical genre on its own terms — narrative, law, psalm, prophecy, parable, epistle. Explains why a passage means what it means, not just what it means.

books.title: 40 Questions About Interpreting the Bible
books.author: Robert L. Plummer
books.description: A question-and-answer reference covering interpretation, from how to handle difficult texts to what the church has historically done with them. Useful to consult rather than to read straight through.

books.title: Ephesians for Everyone
books.author: N. T. Wright
books.description: Wright's own translation with short, accessible commentary section by section. Written for readers with no training, and suited to personal study or a small group working through the letter.

groups.title: New Members: What Does It Mean to Be a Church Member?

books.title: What Is a Healthy Church?
books.author: Mark Dever
books.description: Dever's short account of what a church is for and what marks one that is functioning as it should. The starting point of the nine marks framework.

books.title: What Is a Healthy Church Member?
books.author: Thabiti M. Anyabwile
books.description: The companion volume, turning the question from the institution to the individual. Describes what it looks like to be a member who actually contributes to a church's health.

books.title: Church Membership
books.author: Jonathan Leeman
books.description: Makes the case that membership is a real commitment to a particular body of people rather than an administrative formality. Short, and directly useful to someone deciding whether to join.

groups.title: How Can I Learn More About Who God Is?

books.title: More Than a Carpenter
books.author: Josh McDowell
books.description: A brief apologetic centred on the identity and resurrection of Jesus, written from McDowell's own move from skepticism. Frequently given away because it can be read in a sitting.

books.title: It Is Well
books.author: Mark Dever and Michael Lawrence
books.description: Fourteen expositions on substitutionary atonement, working from Exodus through the Gospels and epistles. Preached sermons rather than a systematic treatment, so it reads more warmly than the subject suggests.

books.title: The Cross of Christ
books.author: John R. W. Stott
books.description: Stott's major work, and the standard modern treatment of the crucifixion — what happened, what it achieved and what it asks of those who accept it. Substantial and rewarding.

books.title: In His Image
books.author: Jen Wilkin
books.description: Ten attributes of God that Christians are called to reflect rather than admire from a distance. A companion to Wilkin's None Like Him, and written for study alone or in a group.

books.title: Good News for Weary Women
books.author: Elyse M. Fitzpatrick
books.description: Fitzpatrick names the extra rules Christian women are handed about marriage, motherhood and appearance, and sets them against what the gospel actually requires. Written for exhaustion rather than for improvement.

books.title: The Set-Apart Woman
books.author: Leslie Ludy
books.description: Ludy argues for a life deliberately set apart for God and works through what gets in the way — distraction, comparison, comfort. Devotional in tone and direct in its challenge.

books.title: Having a Mary Heart in a Martha World
books.author: Joanna Weaver
books.description: Built on the Luke 10 account of the two sisters, for women caught between service and stillness. A long-running favourite in women's groups, with study questions included.

books.title: Women of the Word
books.author: Jen Wilkin
books.description: A method book: how to study the Bible with both heart and mind rather than looking for a feeling. Wilkin teaches comprehension before interpretation before application.

books.title: The Well-Watered Woman
books.author: Gretchen Saffles
books.description: Saffles writes about rootedness in Scripture as the alternative to running dry, mixing teaching with her own account. Reflective, and structured around gospel fullness, transformation and obedience.

books.title: The Emotionally Healthy Woman
books.author: Geri Scazzero
books.description: Scazzero names eight things she had to quit — being afraid of what others think, lying, dying to the wrong things — to become spiritually and emotionally whole. Unusually candid.

books.title: The Masculine Mandate
books.author: Richard D. Phillips
books.description: Phillips builds a definition of biblical manhood from Genesis 2, working outward to a man's role in marriage, family, church and work. Argues from the text rather than from culture.

books.title: Disciplines of a Godly Man
books.author: R. Kent Hughes
books.description: A wide-ranging book on the habits that shape a man's character — purity, marriage, fatherhood, friendship, mind, work, prayer. Includes a study guide and is often used in men's groups.

books.title: The Dude's Guide to Manhood
books.author: Darrin Patrick
books.description: Patrick works through what a man is meant to be — determined, dependable, disciplined, faithful — in short, plainly written chapters. Aimed at men who would not usually pick up a Christian book.

books.title: Raising Men, Not Boys
books.author: Mike Fabarez
books.description: On raising sons toward maturity and responsibility rather than prolonged adolescence. Fabarez writes for parents wanting a long view of what they are actually forming.

books.title: Marriage Matters
books.author: Winston T. Smith
books.description: A counsellor's book on the ordinary moments where marriages are actually made or lost. Practical, focused on daily interaction rather than on principles held at a distance.

books.title: The Meaning of Marriage
books.author: Timothy Keller
books.description: Keller, with Kathy Keller, on marriage as covenant rather than contract — what it is for, why it is hard, and how the gospel bears on it. Includes a chapter addressed to single readers.

books.title: Love That Lasts
books.author: Gary Ricucci and Betsy Ricucci
books.description: Gary and Betsy Ricucci write from long marriage on communication, conflict, romance and forgiveness. Warm and concrete, with the kind of specificity that comes from having done it.

books.title: Sacred Marriage
books.author: Gary Thomas
books.description: Thomas's question is whether God designed marriage to make us holy more than to make us happy. Reframes the difficulties as formation rather than as evidence something has gone wrong.

books.title: You and Me Forever
books.author: Francis Chan and Lisa Chan
books.description: Francis and Lisa Chan argue that a marriage aimed only at itself will disappoint, and that couples do better aimed together at something beyond them. Short chapters, written jointly.

books.title: Loving Him Well
books.author: Gary Thomas
books.description: A revision of Thomas's earlier Sacred Influence, on how a wife actually shapes her husband. Practical, and honest that influence is not the same as control.

books.title: Gospel-Centered Family
books.author: Tim Chester and Ed Moll
books.description: Chester and Ed Moll on ordering family life around grace rather than around performance or control. Short, practical, and written to be used by parents rather than studied.

groups.title: How Can I Be a Christian at Work?

books.title: Every Good Endeavor
books.author: Timothy Keller
books.description: Keller on why work matters to God, why it frustrates us, and how the gospel changes the way it is done. The fullest treatment of vocation on this list.

books.title: The Call
books.author: Os Guinness
books.description: Guinness on calling as the organising centre of a life — not just a job, but the whole of what a person is for. Reflective, drawing widely on history and biography.

books.title: Work Matters
books.author: Tom Nelson
books.description: Nelson argues that Sunday and Monday belong to the same life, and that pastors have often failed to connect them. Written by a pastor correcting his own earlier teaching.

books.title: Work
books.author: Daniel M. Doriani
books.description: A biblical theology of work covering purpose, dignity and transformation, including the harder questions about difficult jobs and unjust workplaces. More systematic than the others here.

groups.title: How Can I Share My Faith?

books.title: Honest Evangelism
books.author: Rico Tice
books.description: Tice is candid that evangelism is uncomfortable and does it anyway. Short, realistic about hostility, and more concerned with courage than with technique.

books.title: Out of the Saltshaker and Into the World
books.author: Rebecca Manley Pippert
books.description: A long-standing classic arguing that evangelism is a way of life rather than an event. Pippert writes about friendship, honesty and asking real questions.

books.title: Learning Evangelism from Jesus
books.author: Jerram Barrs
books.description: Barrs works through the encounters in the Gospels one by one, drawing out how Jesus actually spoke to people. A study of method by observation rather than by rule.

books.title: The Gospel and Personal Evangelism
books.author: Mark Dever
books.description: Dever answers the practical questions directly: who should evangelise, what the message is, and what does not count as evangelism. Brief and clarifying.

books.title: The Conviction to Lead
books.author: R. Albert Mohler
books.description: Twenty-five principles arguing that leadership begins with conviction rather than technique. Mohler writes for people responsible for institutions as well as for teams.

books.title: Spiritual Leadership
books.author: J. Oswald Sanders
books.description: The older classic on this list, and still the most quoted. Sanders sets out the qualifications and cost of spiritual leadership, drawing heavily on biography.

books.title: Spiritual Leadership
books.author: Henry T. Blackaby and Richard Blackaby
books.description: Henry and Richard Blackaby on moving people onto God's agenda rather than the leader's. Written with organisations in view, and often used for elder and staff training.

books.title: Leading with a Limp
books.author: Dan B. Allender
books.description: Allender argues that a leader's brokenness is not a disqualification but the ground of real influence. Counterintuitive, and unusually honest about failure.

books.title: Let the Nations Be Glad!
books.author: John Piper
books.description: Piper's case that worship is both the fuel and the goal of missions. The standard theological argument for why the church sends anyone anywhere.

books.title: What Is the Mission of the Church?
books.author: Kevin DeYoung and Greg Gilbert
books.description: DeYoung and Greg Gilbert ask what the church is actually sent to do, and press on whether social justice, cultural renewal and evangelism are the same task. Argumentative in a useful way.

books.title: Christian Mission in the Modern World
books.author: John R. W. Stott
books.description: Stott takes five contested words — mission, evangelism, dialogue, salvation, conversion — and defines each carefully. A short book that settles a lot of vocabulary.

groups.title: Why Am I So Anxious and Worried?

books.title: Emotionally Healthy Spirituality
books.author: Peter Scazzero
books.description: Scazzero's argument that it is not possible to be spiritually mature while remaining emotionally immature. Written after his own breakdown, and the root of a wider body of material.

books.title: When I Am Afraid
books.author: Edward T. Welch
books.description: A guided workbook rather than a book to read through, taking fear and anxiety a step at a time. Designed to be worked slowly, alone or with a counsellor.

books.title: Running Scared
books.author: Edward T. Welch
books.description: Welch on fear, worry and rest, moving through the specific things people are afraid of — money, people, death — and what Scripture says to each. Substantial and pastoral.

groups.title: What Do I Do with My Shame?

books.title: The Soul of Shame
books.author: Curt Thompson
books.description: Thompson, a psychiatrist, brings neuroscience and Scripture together on how shame forms and how it is undone in relationship. The most clinically grounded book on this list.

books.title: Unashamed
books.author: Heather Davis Nelson
books.description: Nelson on the difference between guilt and shame, and how the gospel addresses the second. Foreword by Edward Welch, which is why the old site listed it under his name.

books.title: Shame Interrupted
books.author: Edward T. Welch
books.description: Welch's fuller treatment of shame — where it comes from, how it operates, and what Christ does about it. Longer and more thorough than Unashamed, and often read after it.

books.title: The Good News About Injustice
books.author: Gary A. Haugen
books.description: Written by the founder of International Justice Mission, on why Christians should expect to act against injustice and what that has looked like in practice. The entry point to this section.

books.title: The Locust Effect
books.author: Gary A. Haugen
books.description: Haugen and Victor Boutros argue that the poor cannot escape poverty while everyday violence goes unpoliced, and that aid has largely ignored this. The most data-driven book here.

books.title: The Insanity of God
books.author: Nik Ripken
books.description: Ripken's account of interviewing believers in persecuted countries after his own faith collapsed on the mission field. Narrative rather than argument, and difficult in places.

books.title: Generous Justice
books.author: Timothy Keller
books.description: Keller on why the biblical case for doing justice runs through grace rather than guilt, and why that changes how it is sustained. Short, and a good bridge for skeptical readers.

books.title: Shrewd Samaritan
books.author: Bruce Wydick
books.description: An economist asks which forms of helping actually help. Wydick tests common assumptions about aid against evidence, without arguing anyone should do less.

books.title: Ministries of Mercy
books.author: Timothy Keller
books.description: Keller's earliest book, on how a local church organises practical mercy — who it serves, how, and where the limits are. Written for churches rather than for individuals.

books.title: The Color of Compromise
books.author: Jemar Tisby
books.description: A historical account of the American church's complicity in racism, from slavery through the civil rights era to the present. Tisby's case is documentary rather than rhetorical.

books.title: Divided by Faith
books.author: Michael O. Emerson and Christian Smith
books.description: Emerson and Christian Smith's sociological study of why American evangelicals, sincerely opposed to racism, have tended to reinforce racial division. Research-based, and frequently cited since.

books.title: Woke Church
books.author: Eric Mason
books.description: Mason calls the church to be aware, awakened and accountable on questions of justice, arguing the case from Scripture. Written by a pastor to other pastors.

books.title: Just Mercy
books.author: Bryan Stevenson
books.description: Stevenson's account of founding the Equal Justice Initiative and defending Walter McMillian, wrongly sentenced to death. Memoir rather than theology, and the basis for the 2019 film.
